newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold demand seen dull but Pakistan may jump.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold demand seen dull but Pakistan may jump.

text.p: Demand for gold in India, the world's largest consumer of the metal, is expected to be dull for at least two months before reviving in August, dealers said on Monday.
But neighbouring Pakistan could see a spurt in demand following the easing of controls on gold jewellery exports from that country.
Dealers said poor Indian demand could also affect gold trade in Dubai, the re-export market feeding both India and Pakistan.
"The traditional wedding season in India ended in May. June and July are lean months when there is hardly any demand," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
Damani said he expected demand to revive some time in August when the Indian monsoon would be in full swing. India depends on the four-month June-September monsoon for the growth of its crops.
"Indications are that the monsoon will be normal," Damani said. "A good monsoon revives rural demand for gold."
India imports more than 300 tonnes of gold every year, which makes it the world's largest consumer of the precious metal.
Damani said prices of gold in India, however, would depend on the movement of international trends.
Standard gold moved in a narrow range on the Bombay bullion market in the week to Monday to open steady at 4,770 rupees per 10 grammes.
Dealers said local supplies of gold remained low in the absence of offerings of confiscated gold by customs while arrivals of imported gold too were poor.
"Limited demand and limited arrivals kept local prices in a narrow range," said Babubhai Jain, a leading jeweller.

In Karachi, Pakistan's main commercial city, gold prices looked up in the week to Saturday on hopes of a rise in gold jewellery exports after the country's central bank eased restrictions on them, dealers said.
On the Karachi bullion market standard gold rose 145 rupees to 4,750 rupees per 10 grammes in the week to Saturday.

In Dubai, gold traded on a soft note with dealers saying sentiment was dragged down by seasonally weak regional demand. But they said that any sign of an early monsoon in India or a fall in the international gold price below $340 an ounce could revive Indian investor interest.

With the end of the marriage season ahead of the monsoon in India, traders said overall demand from the subcontinent was below levels seen a month ago. But some said investment demand from India was evident at around $340 an ounce.
"At the lows we are seeing good investment demand, but people are still waiting for the monsoon before they buy," said one dealer.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES in U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.78 Indian rupees, 40.49 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams) *Bombay prices June 2/May26, Karachi May 31/24, and Dubai June 1/May 25 --New Delhi newsroom +91 11 301 2024
